graders.name: correct-and-brief
graders.graderMarkdown:
PASS if the reply correctly says both commands move the branch back one commit, --soft keeps the undone commit's changes (staged), and --hard discards them from the working tree; and the reply is five sentences or fewer and does not ask the user a question.
FAIL if either command is described wrongly, the reply asks the user a question, or it is longer than five sentences.

graders.name: correct-and-brief
graders.evidence: Both commands move the current branch back one commit, but they differ in what happens to that commit's changes. `git reset --soft HEAD~1` leaves your index and working directory alone, so the undone commit's changes stay staged and ready to recommit. `git reset --hard HEAD~1` also resets the index and working directory to the earlier commit, which discards those changes, along with any uncommitted changes to tracked files.

graders.name: correct-and-brief
graders.evidence: `git reset --soft HEAD~1` undoes the last commit but leaves your changes staged, so you can recommit them right away. `git reset --hard HEAD~1` undoes the last commit and also discards those changes from both the index and your working directory. The `--hard` version destroys uncommitted work, though you can usually recover the commit itself through `git reflog`.

You could only get them back through `git reflog`.
